analyzed_vuln.description: The Bink decoder accepts SCALED_BLOCK at the right or bottom edge without verifying that a full 2x2 group of 8x8 block slots remains. A scaled block produces 16x16 output; for the FILL_BLOCK subtype, bink_decode_plane calls fill_block_tab[0](dst, ..., stride, 16), which writes 16 bytes on each of 16 rows. When bx+1 >= bw or by+1 >= bh, that operation extends beyond the decoded plane allocation, causing the heap-buffer-overflow observed in fill_block16_c. The existing odd bx/by handling only skips presumed continuation slots and does not reject a scaled block beginning at an incomplete edge position.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A fuzzed Bink context supplies attacker-controlled dimensions/metadata through the final 1024-byte fuzzer control trailer and compressed packet bits through the packet prefix. The dimensions produce a plane whose ceil-divided 8x8 block grid has an incomplete 16x16 region at an edge (in particular, an odd bw and/or bh), and the packet decodes the corresponding terminal block as SCALED_BLOCK with FILL_BLOCK subtype. bink_decode_plane then computes dst for that edge block and performs an unconditional 16x16 fill; the PoV reaches this path during decode_frame and writes past the frame plane buffer.

args: Analyze why the supplied Bink PoV could still reach fill_block16_c after adding an edge check `if (bx + 1 >= bw || by + 1 >= bh) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;` at the start of `case SCALED_BLOCK` in ffmpeg/libavcodec/bink.c bink_decode_plane. Pay particular attention to integer dimensions, chroma/luma bw and bh, frame allocation/cropping, and whether a nominal complete 2x2 block-slot group can nevertheless exceed the actual allocated visible plane.

The original ASan report is a heap-buffer-overflow in fill_block16_c called by bink_decode_plane's SCALED_BLOCK/FILL_BLOCK path. I patched ffmpeg/libavcodec/bink.c at the start of the SCALED_BLOCK switch case to reject `bx + 1 >= bw || by + 1 >= bh`. Validation still reports the identical sanitizer dedup. Existing code computes luma bw as ceil(width/8), bh as ceil(height/8), chroma bw as ceil(width/16), bh as ceil(height/16), and visible plane width/height with right shifts. The loop addresses `dst = data + 8*by*stride + 8*bx`; scaled output writes 16x16. Existing odd bx/by SCALED_BLOCK handling skips continuation slots before the switch. Determine whether dimensions not aligned to 8 mean the final nominal slots include padding insufficient for 16 output, or whether another logic issue lets this bypass the check, and recommend a root-cause-safe bounds condition.

Explain concretely how fill_block16_c can nevertheless overflow under tools/target_dec_fuzzer.c's fuzz_get_buffer2. Inspect the allocator and AVFrame buffer relationships. Is frame->linesize later modified independently of the allocated buffer? Does av_frame_get_plane_buffer return a buffer whose size spans inaccessible gaps or multiple planes? Could fill_block16_c use a stride or number of rows differing from assumed? Recommend a minimal reliable decoder-side fix for the reported edge SCALED_BLOCK vulnerability.

Current patches are in ffmpeg/libavcodec/bink.c around lines 1101-1125. Validation repeatedly returns identical `__asan_memset--fill_block16_c--bink_decode_plane`. The direct FILL call remains `c->bdsp.fill_block_tab[0](dst, v, stride, 16)`. The vulnerability report specifically says reject SCALED_BLOCK when bx+1>=bw or by+1>=bh and identifies odd bw/bh terminal blocks. Yet that exact check seemingly has no effect, suggesting perhaps testing uses a different source path/build artifact or the edge slot logic has bx/by mutations. Please inspect exact semantics, including whether bx/bw refer unexpected units for chroma.
